response.rationale: The skin ulcers, palmar lichenoid papules, vasculopathic biopsy, elevated ferritin, lymphocytopenia, and progressive interstitial lung disease fit amyopathic dermatomyositis, especially the anti-MDA5 phenotype; normal strength and depressed CK do not exclude this. SLE is less specific despite overlapping anti-SSA and lymphopenia.

rejected.why: Overlapping anti-SSA, lymphopenia, alopecia, arthralgias, and anticardiolipin positivity, but lacks the characteristic palmar/MCP ulcerative papules and vasculopathic biopsy pattern; no SLE-specific serologies.
Interstitial lung disease is a complication or associated feature rather than the underlying systemic diagnosis and does not explain the skin ulcers, alopecia, or biopsy vasculopathy.
Only anticardiolipin positivity is present; lupus anticoagulant and anti-beta2-glycoprotein 1 are negative, and clinical thrombotic criteria are not met.
Anti-SSA and ILD overlap, but there are no sicca symptoms or other specific Sjogren features, and it does not explain the ulcerative skin lesions or vasculopathic biopsy.
